name: Fibromuscular Dysplasia of the Renal Arteries

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical features

criteria.description: Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance on angiography of renal arteries
Presence of renovascular hypertension unexplained by other causes
Exclusion of atherosclerotic renal artery disease by clinical and imaging evaluation
Histopathological confirmation showing medial fibroplasia or intimal fibroplasia (rarely performed)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic angiographic findings plus renovascular hypertension with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging; histopathology is rarely obtained.

pathognomonic.notes: Often resistant to standard antihypertensive therapy

pathognomonic.symptomName: String of beads appearance on renal artery angiography
searchTerms: beaded look on kidney artery imaging
string of beads in renal angiogram

common.notes: Heard on auscultation in affected patients
Due to renal ischemia or infarction

occasional.notes: Claudication or limb ischemia if other arteries involved
searchTerms: symptoms of blood flow issues in limbs

occasional.notes: Mild proteinuria due to renal ischemia

rare.notes: Rare complication causing acute flank pain
Due to renal ischemia stimulating renin-angiotensin system

imaging: Catheter-based renal artery angiography showing 'string of beads' pattern
CT angiography or MR angiography demonstrating multifocal arterial stenoses and aneurysms
Duplex ultrasound showing turbulent flow and stenosis
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; familial cases reported but rare
other: Histopathology (if obtained) showing medial fibroplasia with alternating areas of stenosis and aneurysmal dilatation

distinguishingFeatures: Proximal renal artery involvement rather than mid or distal segments
Systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss
Histopathological evidence of vessel wall inflammation
Lack of characteristic 'string of beads' pattern

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe flank pain suggesting renal artery dissection
Rapidly worsening hypertension refractory to multiple medications
Acute kidney injury or rapidly declining renal function
references: Olin JW, Gornik HL, Bacharach JM, et al. Fibromuscular Dysplasia: State of the Science and Critical Unanswered Questions: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2014;129(9):1048-1078.
